qs.q: A patient with Hashimoto's thyroiditis typically exhibits which of the following histological features?
o: Dense lymphocytic infiltration with germinal centers and Hürthle cell change
Psammoma bodies and overlapping nuclei with prominent nuclear grooves
Follicular hyperplasia with scalloped colloid and crowded epithelial cells
Granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and central necrosis
qs.e: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is characterized histologically by a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with germinal centers and Hürthle cell metaplasia. Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells is instead seen in De Quervain's subacute thyroiditis.
qs.s: Year 3: Endocrine and Metabolic Pathology: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following best characterizes Riedel's thyroiditis?
o: Lymphocytic infiltration featuring prominent and active germinal centers
Rock-hard thyroid featuring dense fibrous tissue extending beyond the capsule
Follicular hyperplasia featuring scalloped colloid and columnar cells
Painful tender thyroid featuring granulomas and multinucleated giant cells
qs.e: Riedel's thyroiditis is a fibroinflammatory condition replacing the thyroid with keloid-like fibrosis extending into surrounding structures. It presents as a rock-hard fixed neck mass that can mimic malignancy.
qs.s: Year 3: Endocrine and Metabolic Pathology — Part 2: MCQs

qs.q: Which underlying mechanism is responsible for autoimmune-mediated hypothyroidism in Hashimoto’s thyroiditis?
o: Hyperstimulation of pituitary TSH receptors
Immune-mediated destruction of thyroid tissue
Overactivity of intracellular deiodinases
Excessive dietary iodine supplementation
qs.e: Hashimoto’s thyroiditis leads to immune-mediated destruction of thyroid tissue, resulting in decreased hormone output and clinical hypothyroidism. Dietary iodine deficiency is a distinct, non-autoimmune cause of hypothyroidism.

qs.q: An autoimmune thyroid disorder presents with chronic thyroiditis resulting from the immune-mediated destruction of the thyroid gland. What is this condition called?
o: Hashimoto's disease
Thyroid adenoma
Graves' disease
Toxic multinodular goiter
qs.e: Hashimoto's disease is characterized by the autoimmune destruction of the thyroid gland leading to hypothyroidism. Graves' disease involves stimulation by antibodies rather than destruction, resulting in hyperthyroidism.

qs.q: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is associated with antibodies against ---
o: B. Antibodies to T3 and T4 hormones
C. Antibodies to thyroglobulin and thyroid peroxidase
D. Antibodies to thyroid‑stimulating immunoglobulins
A. Antibodies to TSH receptor
qs.e: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is characterized by anti‑thyroglobulin and anti‑thyroid peroxidase antibodies.

qs.q: What is the characteristic sequence of thyroid function tests (TFTs) in subacute (De Quervain's) thyroiditis?
o: Hyperthyroidism to hypothyroidism to recovery
Permanent hypothyroidism from disease onset
Hypothyroidism to hyperthyroidism to recovery
Euthyroid throughout the disease course
qs.e: Subacute thyroiditis typically follows a triphasic course: an initial hyperthyroid phase (due to release of preformed thyroid hormone), followed by a hypothyroid phase (as thyroid hormone stores are depleted), and finally recovery to euthyroidism in most cases. It is often preceded by a viral upper respiratory infection and is associated with a markedly elevated ESR and very low radioactive iodine uptake.
